text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Junior finance minister Wim Vermeend is to attack closed investment funds. (p1)
- The three top financial market supervisory bodies step up cooperation possibly leading to a merger. (p1)
- Dutch natural gas production and distribution monopoly Gasunie appears to be strengthening its role as a gas banker. (p1)
- Engineering concern Stork seeks the help of temp agencies to make its workforce more flexible. (p3)
- Engineering sector criticises discontinuation of subsidies for companies exporting capital goods to developing countries. (p3).
- Livestock transporters demand more money for moving swine fever infected pigs. (p2)
- Real estate and technical wholesale firm Air Holding sells its car unit Ford Wilton to Japan's Sumitomo. (p2)
- Radiation during KLM flights of diagnostic tools too low for passengers to claim damages. (p3)
- ABN Amro Asset Management's investments rose by 25 million guilders, or 21 percent, in first six months of this year. (p11)
- Lightning paralyses railways in the Randstad, the Netherlands' urban heartland. (p1)
- Number of bankruptcies in first half of 1997 up six percent compared with same period of 1996. (p39)
